findings.title: A `null` identity entry becomes `{}`, so an identity marked for removal gets assigned instead.
findings.body:
In ARM PATCH, `userAssignedIdentities: {<id>: null}` is the standard way to remove one user-assigned identity. `clean_null_values(None)` returns `None`, and the new `or {}` turns that into `{}`.

Trigger: a YAML manifest with `"<id>": null` under `userAssignedIdentities`, passed to `update --yaml`.

Before this change the entry was silently dropped. Now it is sent as `{}`, which asks the service to keep or add the identity: the opposite of what the manifest says.

I could not check whether this PATCH endpoint treats `null` as removal.

Fix: only replace an identity's value with `{}` when the original value is a dict. Keep an explicit `None` as `None`, and make the outer filter keep `None` values inside `userAssignedIdentities`. Or, at minimum, leave the old behaviour of dropping such entries, and don't turn them into assignments.
